body.name: distinct truncated-factorization and fixing operators
body.construction:
Fix the topological order \(\prec\) encoded by \(I\).  For a positive finite kernel \(q\) and an ordered vertex set \(B\), \(\operatorname{TF}_{\prec}(q,B)\) is the product of the chain-rule factors
\[
 q\{X=x\mid \operatorname{pre}_{\prec}(X)=x_{\operatorname{pre}_{\prec}(X)}\},
 \qquad X\in B,
\]
obtained solely by finite marginalization and conditioning.  It changes neither the graph nor the fixed set and has no fixability premise.  In contrast, if \(\pi=\operatorname{fixSeq}_G(T)\ne\operatorname{none}\), then \(\operatorname{Fix}(G,q,\pi)\) applies the CADMG fixing operator in the computed order.  At a current vertex \(W\), it forms from current-kernel marginals the actual nested-Markov conditional
\[
 q\{W\mid \operatorname{nd}_{G}(W),\operatorname{fixed}(G)\},
\]
divides the current kernel by that conditional, and removes every arrowhead into \(W\).  Every marginalization and division is returned with its ledger data; no fixing operation is called before a valid sequence has been computed.
